identity.title: VALES - III. The calibration between the dust continuum and interstellar gas content of star-forming galaxies
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: We use CO(1–0) observations from the Atacama Large Millimetre/submillimetre Array (ALMA) to trace the molecular gas mass, $M_{\mathrm{H}_{2}}$

question.value: What is the calibration between the 850 um dust continuum luminosity and the molecular/ISM gas mass for 67 main-sequence star-forming galaxies at 0.02<z<0.35, and does it agree with Scoville et al. 2016?

evidence.quote: We present the calibration between the dust continuum luminosity and interstellar gas content obtained from the Valparaíso ALMA Line Emission Survey (VALES) sample of 67 main-sequence star-forming galaxies at $0.02<z<0.35$.
This paper uses the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA #2012.1.01080.S & #2013.1.00530.S.

evidence.quote: Whilst we recommend using this best-fit calibration rather than the constant calibration

why_this_method.value: Dust continuum is faster than line observations for ISM mass at high z

evidence.quote: being much faster ($\sim$ 20$\times$) at estimating the ISM mass than molecular line observations

limitations_admitted.value: Largest uncertainty is alpha_CO; few resolved galaxies

evidence.quote: we stress that the largest uncertainty in this work remains in the $\alpha_{\rm CO}$ factor.
